## Analysis Summary

- Green soybean leaf (upper surface)
- ~20–30 scattered discrete lesions
- Dark brown centers, irregular to roughly circular
- Several lesions surrounded by clear **yellow/pale halos**
- Varying sizes (~3–10mm), well-defined margins

**Key differentiators:**
- **Bacterial_Pustule** KB: "A greenish-yellow halo surrounds each lesion" — the yellow halos in the test image strongly match this descriptor. Lesions are irregular, scattered on green leaf (upper surface view; pustules form on lower surface, not visible here).
- **Frogeye_leaf_spot**: Described as gray center with reddish-brown border — the test image lesions lack the distinctive gray/lighter center; centers appear uniformly dark brown.
- **Septoria_brown_spot**: Typically smaller, denser spots with general leaf yellowing; early-stage Septoria reference (bottom-right panel) shows smaller more numerous lesions, not matching.
- **Bacterial_Blight**: Angular lesions following veins, often causing tattered appearance — not present here.
- Other candidates (Cercospora, SDS, Vein necrosis, Anthracnose, TSV) clearly do not match the discrete brown-spot-with-halo pattern.

The **yellow halos surrounding dark brown lesions on the upper leaf surface** is the most discriminating feature, pointing clearly to **Bacterial_Pustule**.
